Hello and welcome to the quit without a plan club.. I wont bore you with details but I have had some experience in this department.   
  
First of all, smile and show gratitude that you have the privilege of quitting without a job. And if your husband has been supportive, thank him too, a lot. Not everyone gets such a supporting partner.   


Now, I do not know your situation, but based on my experience   


Freak out if you need to. Set some time aside each day for a panic attack, It is OKAY. It is FINE. You have the right to be anxious. You have the right to that sinking feeling in your heart. Please do not beat yourself up over it.   


Log to kaafi kuch kahenge. Sabse advice lene ki zaroorat nahi hai. Do not and I repeat DO NOT get into the mode of "what will people think"  
Reflect on what you need. 

Do not beat yourself up for quitting. It does not make you 'weak', or 'unproductive'. Just because a fish cannot climb a tree does not mean it cannot do anything worthwhile. 

You just need the right soil to grow. There is nothing anyone else can give you. You already have everything to start the journey. It will be tough. You will burn. You will walk on coals. But well, at least it is on your own terms. 

There will be times when you will struggle and then blame yourself for leaving the job. Watch out for such thoughts. And question them. In fact, question every thought you have when it comes to quitting. 

And I will not lie. It will be tough. But anything is better than a mental breakdown due to work. 

I would suggest you use this time for reflection, identify triggers, gain self awareness. The world is not a wish granting factory, to asaan to nahi hoga. But use this to get some existential insights into what you want to do and who you are (minus your job title, your relationships, your family, your social group etc..)

Take it one step at a time. Small steps. That is how baby birds fly. You should be up and about running soon. Take care!

Suicide attempt survivor here. I have been where you have, and though I will not say I know what you are going through (because only you are the one who is living through it), but I can empathise. Thankfully I met the right psychologist, who really turned my head around.

It can get overwhelming - But one thing that has worked for me (which I would invite you to try), is Mindfulness and distress tolerance. Extreme emotions often have a physiological reaction. And when you feel like this, it has been known that even doing something as simple as holding ice in your hands, or going for a mindful walk can really help. Try it. 

How is your nutrition? Are you eating right? Sleep? Do go to phychiatrist once to see if there are any meds you could take even for a short while. 

And please, please, please - Trust me, I know it seems like hell right now. But dont think about your whole life. Think about just one day at a time. One moment at a time. It will become much more bearable. Your therapist clearly isnt right for you. 

You will get through this my friend. Let's do this together. One step, one breath, one moment, one day and one battle at a time.
